note: sha256 of the files shared with can-slim-recommend. TWO CLASSES, and conflating them caused a real regression: 'verbatim' files carry no local extensions, so a byte difference IS drift; 'substance' files legitimately differ, because each side adds its own material, and demanding equal bytes there does not detect drift but manufactures it - the only way to go green is to delete the other side's work, which is exactly what happened (sister commit 6e281fb wholesale-copied both substance files and destroyed its own 'Modern refinements' section and its --asof truncation). Substance is checked by behaviour instead: the sister's scripts/check_parity.py requires every canonical rung paragraph to appear verbatim in its copy and runs BOTH relative_strength implementations over shared series demanding identical numbers. Update hashes ONLY in the same commit that ports the change.

owed_from_sister.commit: (owed to this repo, from the sister)
owed_from_sister.summary: scripts/check_parity.py - a CROSS-REPO behavioural parity check
owed_from_sister.why: This repo's check_parity.py hashes files in its own tree and says outright that it cannot see a reworded threshold. The sister's reads BOTH checkouts and tests behaviour in five layers: shared bytes split verbatim/substance; shared substance (canonical rungs verbatim + both relative_strength copies run over 60 shared series demanding identical numbers); the two dashboards' REAL scoring code lifted from the templates and run in node over all 3^7 = 2187 scorecards; 100 random tickers with messy authored input; and the methodology's rungs checked against what the code implements. It compiles modules from source text rather than importing them, because a stale __pycache__ made it report a maths divergence between two byte-identical functions - and would equally have hidden a real one.

owed_from_sister.commit: (owed to this repo, from the sister)
owed_from_sister.summary: scripts/annual_eps.py - grade A from SEC XBRL annual EPS
owed_from_sister.why: A asks for EPS up EACH of 3 years at >=25%, and TradingView's get_financial_history returns 8 quarters whatever period is requested - two fiscal years, one short - so A cannot be graded from the connector at all and TTM growth is a different test (AVT reads +46% TTM while its FY2025 EPS fell 49%). Five traps are documented in it, including that XBRL's `fy` is the FILING's fiscal focus so keying on it shuffles years (MU came out with its FY2023 loss labelled FY2025), and that filers change EPS tag over time so tags must be merged in preference order, not raced.
